facts.fact_text: Following Mr Aleksey Navalnyy's call, on Sunday 26 March 2017, thousands of people took to the streets in more than eighty Russian cities protesting against corruption, lawlessness and inequality.
On 26 March 2017, Mr Navalnyy arrived in Tverskaya street to take part in the march.
On 26 March 2017, Mr Navalnyy was walking down Tverskaya street with other participants of the march.
At 2.28 p.m. on 26 March 2017, Mr Navalnyy was apprehended by the police in Tverskaya street and placed in a police bus.
At 3.31 p.m. on 26 March 2017, Mr Navalnyy was administratively arrested at the Konkovo police station of Moscow.
On 27 March 2017, the Tverskoy District Court of Moscow found Mr Navalnyy guilty of organising and holding an unauthorised public event with about 4,000 participants.
The Tverskoy District Court of Moscow sentenced Mr Navalnyy to a fine of 20,000 Russian roubles for organising and holding an unauthorised public event on 26 March 2017.
The Tverskoy District Court of Moscow found Mr Navalnyy guilty of breach of Article 19.3 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offence (failure to obey a lawful order of a police officer).
The Tverskoy District Court of Moscow sentenced Mr Navalnyy to 15 days' administrative detention for breach of Article 19.3 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offence.

The offence of organising and holding an unauthorised public event causing disruption of movement of pedestrians and traffic is punishable under Article 20.2 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offence.
The unauthorised public event for which Mr Navalnyy was found guilty caused disruption of movement of pedestrians and traffic.

On 22 March 2017, the Regional Security and Anti-Corruption Department of Moscow suggested to Mr Navalnyy that he hold his public events in Sokolniki park, located quite far from the centre of Moscow.

On 22 March 2017, the Regional Security and Anti-Corruption Department of Moscow suggested to Mr Navalnyy that he hold his public events in Lublino district, located quite far from the centre of Moscow.
The Moscow City Court refused to question the eyewitnesses of Mr Navalnyy's arrest on appeal.
The Moscow City Court disallowed Mr Navalnyy's questions to the police officers during their examination on appeal.
